provenance.notes: Our contribution: the irregular 5x12 "pair-complement-2" base template on which the pair-partition rule is applied (the 12 block columns form 6 column pairs; each of the 5 block rows contains all pairs but two, so every check has weight 8; the left-out pairs form a triangle and a path on the 6 pairs, so two pairs have qubit degree 4 and the rest degree 3; the same template on both sides; design rate 1/6); the census of this family (every placement of 5 left-out pair sets per side, 259 X/Z classes up to symmetry, ranked by a permanent-vector upper bound, our generalisation of App. A of arXiv:2609.30069 to sparse templates); the couple solver that found its exponent spaces (an exact depth-first search over the pairings of every X-row/Z-row overlap, restricted to pairings invariant under one automorphism of the template so that it either finds solutions or exhausts; here an order-3 automorphism gave 12 solutions in under a minute, after 777 annealing tries had found none); the choice of this pairing, the lift P = 83 and this exponent draw; and the distance screening described in notes/996-166-32.md. Construction framework, not ours: the pair-partition construction and its paired-difference equations on CPM exponents are Okada and Kasai's (arXiv:2607.14091), where they are applied to complete J x L templates; the design-rate count R = 1 - J_tot/L_stab and the permanent-vector bound (their App. A) are from Lee, Okada, Maskara, Kasai and Zhou (arXiv:2609.30069), whose outlook names quantum-compatible irregular templates as a natural direction; this entry is one instance in that direction. Quasi-cyclic CSS LDPC codes from circulant permutation matrices go back to Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:quant-ph/0701020), and CSS pairs of two irregular LDPC codes were analysed by Hagiwara and Imai (arXiv:0801.1361). Board precedents of the same commutation rule at weight 8 on the complete (3,8) template include codes/912-234-22.json by @jacksongquera, codes/904-230-22.json by @vprusso (which also cites the lifted-product construction of Panteleev and Kalachev, arXiv:2111.03654) and the published codes/584-150-18.json (Okada-Kasai); our codes/990-198-17.json applies the rule to a different irregular template with weight-7 checks, and our pending PR #4035 (https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/qldpc-challenge/pull/4035) to the 4x10 "pair-complement" template (all pairs but one) at rate 1/5. In our check for codes/990-198-17.json (2026-10-22: arXiv:2607.14091, arXiv:2609.30069, the Okada-Kasai project page, web searches) we did not find a pair-partition code on an irregular template; literature novelty is not claimed. Distance: a witness-backed upper bound (confidence upper_bound), d <= 32; no lower bound is claimed. Stern information-set decoding found weight-32 logicals on both sides and nothing lighter in 9 runs per side (60 s to 1 h each; the deepest: 2 seeds x 1 h per side, about 511000 iterations each, 32 on all four); per-run results ranged from 32 to 44, so the search had not settled at shorter run times. The board's verify/heuristic_distance.py (RIS, orbit pass over 1 symmetry partition, 400000 gf2_fast trials, seed 3) returned 'inconclusive': its lightest logicals had weight 72 (X) and 100 (Z), so at this size it did not get down to the claimed 32 and found nothing lighter. Details in notes/996-166-32.md.
